args.text:
Southern Cornbread's a hearty cornbread with no sugar in it, and they serve it all over the Southeastern United States. It's easy to make, and it usually turns up as the bread with lunch or tea (supper). Plenty of people over there will even make a quick, simple feed of it now and then (brekkie, even) by crumbling cornbread into a glass of buttermilk and tucking in.

Ingredients

2 cups yellow or white self-raising cornmeal

1 large egg

1¼–1½ cups buttermilk or full-cream milk

¼ cup olive oil or vegetable oil

Equipment

A well-seasoned 8-inch (20 cm) or 10-inch (25 cm) cast-iron frying pan (or if you haven't got one: an ovenproof frying pan or an 8x8-inch (20 x 20 cm) baking tin)

A few measuring cups

A medium or large mixing bowl

Method

Crank the oven up to 425°F (220°C). If you're using the cast-iron pan, whack it in the oven to heat up too. Don't preheat any other sort of frying pan or baking tin, mind.

If you're using a frying pan or tin that isn't cast iron, give it a good squirt of spray oil.

Beat the egg in the bowl, then stir in the buttermilk and oil.

Stir in the cornmeal and mix till it's only just wet through. The batter'll be a bit lumpy, and that's fine. Go easy and don't overmix it.

Pour the batter into the pan and pop it in the oven.

Bake till the crust's a light golden brown and a toothpick poked into the centre comes out clean. In an 8-inch (20 cm) pan that can take 25–30 minutes; in a 10-inch (25 cm) pan or an 8x8-inch (20 x 20 cm) tin, about 20–25 minutes.

Let it cool for 5 minutes in the pan before you serve it up.

Notes, tips and variations

If there's any cornbread left over, wrap it in a damp tea towel (keeps it moist) and it'll keep in the fridge for several days. You can freeze it in freezer bags for several months, but it'll usually go a bit more crumbly that way.
